key_insight: Physics-informed machine learning can accurately predict cRPA-derived Hubbard parameters (Ueff, V, J) for transition-metal oxides while retaining interpretable links to electronic structure and chemistry.
engineering_relevance: The models can accelerate beyond-DFT screening and materials design by replacing expensive cRPA calculations with fast, transferable estimates of correlation parameters.
method: Train ensemble-learning regressors on physically motivated descriptors.
Use a regression-based brute-force search to extract explicit analytical formulas.
Include features capturing bandwidth, band-center separation, hybridization, and atomic identity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports low test errors for the ensemble models: RMSE = 0.148 eV for Ueff, 0.062 eV for V, and 0.007 eV for J.
watch_item: Because the models are trained on transition-metal oxides and cRPA labels, transferability to other chemistries or lower-quality descriptor sets may be limited.
paper_title: Physics-informed Machine Learning Prediction of Hubbard Interaction Parameters
